description: Asserts CAS (compare-and-swap) reclamation semantics for expired leases. The 'version' column must increment monotonically on each reclamation attempt; a sweep that reads version=N must supply version=N in its UPDATE WHERE version=N to succeed. Stale sweeps (version mismatch) must fail silently (rows_affected=0).

scenarios.name: successful_cas_reclamation
scenarios.description: Sweep reads lease with version=0, expires_at in the past, state='reserved'; issues UPDATE SET state='settled', version=version+1, reclamation_reason='reserved_ttl_expired' WHERE version=0; rows_affected=1

scenarios.name: stale_sweep_cas_miss
scenarios.description: Two concurrent sweeps both read version=0; first succeeds (version now=1); second issues UPDATE WHERE version=0; rows_affected=0 (CAS miss) — no double-reclamation

scenarios.name: dispatch_committed_at_invariant
scenarios.description: A lease in state='reserved' must have dispatch_committed_at=NULL. Transition to 'prompt_sent' must set dispatch_committed_at. The DB CHECK constraint dispatch_committed_at_set_on_send enforces this.
scenarios.constraint: CONSTRAINT dispatch_committed_at_set_on_send CHECK(lease_state = 'reserved' OR dispatch_committed_at IS NOT NULL)
